tools.name: list_sections

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Lists every site you own, newest first - site_key, name, preview_url and when that preview link expires, whether it is published and on which domain, and when it was created and last changed. Signed in (OAuth) it lists your account; with a draft_token it lists that draft. Read-only and free.

tools.name: archive_site
tools.description: Removes one of your own UNPUBLISHED sites from your account so it no longer appears in list_sites (for example test sites). Nothing is deleted: it is the same recoverable archive the dashboard uses. Live sites, and sites with an active client pay link, are refused. Signed-in accounts only. Free.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Lists every page of a site (home first) with its path, name, draft preview URL and live URL. Use the path as the page parameter of edit_section, add_section, list_sections and the version tools. Free.

tools.name: remove_page
tools.description: Removes one page (not the home page) from your site, using the dashboard's recoverable delete: a version is saved first and the page can be restored. Signed-in accounts only. Free.

tools.name: replace_page_html
tools.description: Re-imports ONE page (the home page too) from new HTML, in place: same address, same share link, same place in the page order, and a version is saved first so it can be undone. Use it to refresh a page built earlier. stage:true previews it before it goes live. Free.

tools.name: prowess_buy_domain
tools.description: Operator token only, during a "code prowess" build the owner authorized with a spending cap. Exact business name within the cap bea

tools.name: publish_status
tools.description: For a domain your site uses: does DNS point at our server, is the HTTPS certificate in place, and does the page answer? live:true means a visitor can open https://<domain> now. A fresh domain usually takes 5-15 minutes; poll every 20-30 seconds.

tools.name: record_review
tools.description: Reviewer token only. Records pass or revise for one exact version of a site (from list_reviews). The operator token can publish only a version whose latest review is a pass; any edit makes a new version.

tools.name: list_reviews
tools.description: For one site: whether publishing with the operator token needs a review (enforced), the current draft and staged versions (what record_review must name), and the reviews recorded so far, newest first.

tools.name: live_check
tools.description: For a published domain of your site: https root 200, http and www reach https://<domain>/ in one hop, title/description/og tags name the site, og:image is a 1200x630 PNG/JPEG, the favicon is the site's own, no editor leftovers, outbound links answer, exactly one h1, no draft badge. Returns PASS/WARN

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: Lists a site's saved versions, newest first - version_id, why it was saved, its label, whether an AI edit made it (ai: true), and when. Every edit_section and set_theme call saves the page first, so any AI edit can be undone with restore_version. Free, and no account is needed for a draft you create

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Puts a site back to a version from list_versions - the undo button for AI edits. The current page is saved as a version first, so a restore can itself be undone. Free, and no account is needed for a draft you created.

tools.name: import_image
tools.description: Copies a photo from a public URL (e.g. the business's own website) into Pagetool's image store and returns its hosted url. tools.name: set_client_record
tools.description: Saves who a site is for and where things stand: business name, contact name/email/phone, the source pages its facts came from, status (prospect, pitched, managed, declined, transferred_out) and notes. Only the fields you pass change; null clears one. list_sites shows each site's record.

tools.name: create_transfer_code
tools.description: Creates a one-time link that hands a managed site to a departing client: they sign in or sign up and accept, and the site (and, by default, its domain) moves to their account. The link works once and expires at expires_at; creating a new one cancels the previous one. Signed-in accounts only.

tools.name: publish_staged
tools.description: Makes a site's staged changes (edit_section/set_theme with stage: true) live. The live page is saved as a version first, so this can be undone with restore_version. Free.

tools.name: discard_staged
tools.description: Drops a site's staged changes without touching the live site. Free.

tools.name: set_theme
tools.description: Repaints the palette and fonts of an existing site across every section without touching its content or structure - the tool for make it warmer, darker, more corporate. At least one of palette_primary, palette_neutral, font_heading, font_body is required. Free, and no account is needed for a draft y

tools.name: get_preview_url
tools.description: Returns the shareable preview URL for a site, plus its expiry. The create tools already return this URL, so call this only when you need it again later. Free, and no account is needed for a draft you created. You can edit or claim this draft for 7 days from creation.

tools.name: draft_create
tools.description: Mints an anonymous draft identity (a draft token) with no account and no sign-in. You usually do NOT need to call this first: create_site_from_brief and create_site_from_html mint one for you and return it. Use this only when you want the token before composing anything. tools.name: export_site_html
tools.description: Renders a site to a single self-contained HTML file. Paying customers only: requires a signed-in bearer token and an entitlement, so anonymous drafts do not export.

tools.name: draft_claim
tools.description: Moves an anonymous draft onto the account of the signed-in user after they have authorized. Call this only once the user has said they want to keep the site - never before, and never as a precondition for building.

tools.name: domain_search
tools.description: Checks availability and price for a domain, or for a bare name across a set of TLDs. Free and needs no account. Use it once the user wants their finished draft on a real address. tools.name: cancel_client_checkout
tools.description: Retires a pay link that has NOT been paid (give code = the pcl_… part of pay_url, or site_key), so nobody can pay it. Nothing is charged. A link that was already paid cannot be cancelled here.

tools.name: rename_site
tools.description: Changes a site's display name (shown in list_sites and the dashboard). Plain text; HTML entities like ' are decoded. Max 120 characters. Signed-in accounts only. Free.

tools.description: Reports who the caller currently is: an authenticated account, an anonymous draft holder, or nobody. Never errors on absent credentials. You do not need to call this before building - building needs no identity at all.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_pages, list_reviews, get_preview_url, purchase_link, upsert_site_form, list_form_submissions · Private data: add_page, prowess_buy_domain, record_review, list_reviews, set_client_record, draft_create, export_site_html, whoami · Public sink: replace_page_html, publish_status, record_review, import_image, set_client_record, publish_staged, purchase_link, upsert_site_form, list_form_submissions, publish_site · Destructive: edit_section, remove_page, purchase_execute, upsert_site_form.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_pages, list_reviews, get_preview_url, purchase_link, upsert_site_form, list_form_submissions · Private data: add_page, prowess_buy_domain, record_review, list_reviews, set_client_record, draft_create, export_site_html, whoami · Public sink: replace_page_html, publish_status, record_review, import_image, set_client_record, publish_staged, purchase_link, upsert_site_form, list_form_submissions, publish_site · Destructive: edit_section, remove_page, purchase_execute, upsert_site_form

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
